subject: Re: NovaHealth POC — streaming UX, model fit & next steps
messages:
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Reena Shah <reena@novahealth.com>, Matt Liu <matt.liu@novahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-15T17:22:00Z
Subject: NovaHealth discovery — post-call recap + immediate asks

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and suggested next steps so we keep momentum for the PoC.

Call highlights:
- Use case: automated discharge summaries (structured + narrative) for 3 hospitals; emphasis on clinical accuracy and hallucination avoidance.
- Success criteria (mutually agreed): 95% factual accuracy on key fields, <3 hallucinations per 1,000 notes, and p95 streaming latency <500ms for 1–2 concurrent clinicians.
- Data constraints: no PHI in logs, customer will use token redaction + KMS for keys.

Model fit / immediate recommendations:
- Start with two model families for evaluation: a smaller low-latency model for quick edits (redwood-rlite-3b-q4) and a higher-quality model for full rewrite/summarization (redwood-std-13b).
- Run a side-by-side stream test to compare partial-output coherence and stop-sequence behavior; streaming can make partial outputs look truncated if stop tokens are not aligned with clinical sentence boundaries.
- Recommended prompt set attached (nova_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) — includes 120 real but redacted examples and scoring prompts.

Streaming UX / quality notes we observed in earlier pilots:
- Partial-output incoherence often appears when the model emits tokens across sentence boundaries and the client renders each chunk without EOS handling.
- Stop-sequence mismatches: for some templates the default newline-based stop caused premature truncation. We recommend adding explicit <EOT> marker in the generation template for comparison.
- Latency trade-offs: batching + KV cache increases throughput but can add 30–80ms; we’ll measure p50/p95 with and without batching.

Immediate next steps (proposal):
1) Redwood runs an initial 48hr canary on your 120-example prompt set (we'll use the attached prompt_set).
2) Ben (SE) will run a focused streaming eval with our script and return p50/p95 latency + partial-render coherence flags.
3) If metrics look good, we provision a 2-week Dedicated trial for the pilot hospitals (quote & SLA attached).

Can you confirm: (a) the attached prompt set is representative, (b) procurement contact (cc'd?) for a short MSA/POC work order?

Attachments: nova_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, poC-sla-proposal.pdf

—
Jasmine Liu

On Mon, Feb 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Reena Shah <reena@novahealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jasmine — great write-up. Quick clarifications:
> - The 120 examples are fine as a starting sample; we'll add 30 more edge cases...

Thanks — attaching an eval script (streaming-eval-script.py) and a short checklist for the canary. Outline of our streaming evaluation plan:
- Measurement: instrumented client that records token arrival timestamps, chunk sizes, and uses a coherence detector to flag incomplete sentences at chunk boundaries.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency (token-level), partial-coherence-rate (percentage of chunks that end mid-sentence), stop-sequence failures (cases where the generated text required trimming by client).
- Stop-token recommendation: add explicit <EOT> and use model-side instruction to avoid newline-only termination. We'll test both "soft" and "hard" stops.
- Quantization note: the q4 family reduces latency but can subtly change tokenization behavior; we'll include side-by-side QA tests focusing on hallucination rates.

I'll run the first pass on Wednesday and share raw metrics + examples where incoherence is visible.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Matt Liu <matt.liu@novahealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, jasmine_liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Reena Shah <reena@novahealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-18T11:55:00Z
Subject: Re: NovaHealth discovery — post-call recap + immediate asks

Appreciate the plan. A couple of follow-ups from engineering:
- The biggest risk we saw in the pilot was partial coherence in long discharge narratives — sentences split across stream chunks created confusing interim displays for clinicians. Will your client-side SDK include an option to buffer until a punctuation token or EOS marker?
- For the quantized models: if q4 changes tokenization behavior (affecting stop tokens), can you provide deterministic examples we can run locally?
- Also curious about how fallback routing works if a higher-quality model exceeds latency SLOs during peak hours — will the platform automatically route to the low-latency variant? What's the observable signal?

If you can share a short canary run (20 notes) with both models and the streaming trace, we’ll review and decide on the Dedicated trial.

-Matt
Senior Software Engineer, NovaHealth

2) Redwood SE (Ben) will run the 48hr canary and a focused 20-note canary (requested by Matt) using both redwood-rlite-3b-q4 and redwood-std-13b. 3) We'll include a deterministic example demonstrating any tokenization differences between q4 vs. standard runs.
4) Product note: our routing policy can be configured to fallback to the low-latency variant when p95 > configured SLO for a short window (policy is observable via the Console and emits events to the tracing hooks). Ben will include the routing event sample in the report.
